name: Opus 5 trend following
strategy: Systematic time-series trend across six sleeves with signals refreshed through the 2026-10-16 close: long only where price is above both the 50- and 200-day moving average with positive 3-month momentum, short only where both are broken and momentum is negative, sized inversely to realised volatility - still the single 2026 macro trend of an energy supply shock into high yields, expressed through duration, energy, housing, the dollar and crypto, with the equity-beta (SPY) sleeve cut after its signal broke.
reassessment_note: I recomputed every sleeve's signal from Yahoo Finance daily closes through 2026-10-16. Those closes match the packet marks exactly. Five of the seven sleeves still pass the rule unchanged. TLT (80.05) is below its 50-day (80.73) and 200-day (84.95) averages, with 3-month momentum of -4.6%: short still valid. ITB (86.40) is below its 50-day (91.52) and 200-day (96.70), at -9.4%: short still valid. XLE (68.24) is above its 50-day (63.54) and 200-day (57.62), at +17.8%: long still valid. USO (161.76) is above its 50-day (142.68) and 200-day (119.26), at +28.9%: long still valid. UUP (28.92) is above its 50-day (28.40) and 200-day (27.84), at +1.9%: long still valid. BTC (81,501) is above its 200-day (72,360) and only barely above its 50-day (81,252), at +29.4%. It still qualifies, so it stays at its small 7% weight. SPY fails the rule: it closed at 763.25, below its 50-day of 768.50, after the 10-14 to 10-16 semiconductor-led selloff, and its 3-month momentum is only +2.9%. The mandate holds a long only where price is above both averages, so the SPY sleeve is closed and its 6% goes to cash at 4% APY rather than being forced into another sleeve. Weights and stops on the other legs are unchanged, to avoid churn costs on signals that have not changed. One risk I am watching is that TLT bounced about 2.7% this week from 77.98. That has not broken the short signal, and the 10% stop is far away. The research was limited. One web search did not return coverage of the 10-16 session itself. It only returned mid-September reports of chip selloffs alongside WTI above $101 and a 10-year yield above 5%, which fit the book's macro thesis. This decision therefore rests mainly on the price-based signal recomputation, not on news.

positions.thesis: Duration short is still the core of the oil-shock / high-yield trend. TLT at 80.05 is below its 50-day (80.73) and 200-day (84.95) averages, with 3-month momentum of -4.6%. Its 20-day volatility is only about 11%, so inverse-vol sizing keeps it the largest sleeve. This week's bounce from 77.98 has not broken the signal, and the 10% stop caps the damage if duration rallies.

The strongest equity trend in the book: XLE at 68.24 is well above its 50-day (63.54) and 200-day (57.62) averages, with 3-month momentum of +17.8%, and the leg is +11% since entry. Energy is the primary expression of the supply-shock trend. Weight held at 20% with a wide 18% stop so a trend this strong is not shaken out by noise.

Housing is the rate-sensitive loser of high yields. ITB at 86.40 is below its 50-day (91.52) and 200-day (96.70) averages, with 3-month momentum of -9.4%. Its 20-day volatility is about 27%, so inverse-vol sizing holds it at 16%. The 15% stop guards against a sharp rate-relief rally.

Crude is the purest trend in the book: USO at 161.76 is above its 50-day (142.68) and 200-day (119.26) averages, with 3-month momentum of +28.9% and a fresh high this week. Its realised volatility of about 38% is the highest of any sleeve, so inverse-vol sizing keeps it at 9%. The 35% take-profit banks a parabolic spike, and the 15% stop protects against a geopolitical reversal.

The weakest qualifying long. BTC at about 81,500 is above its 200-day (72,360) and only marginally above its 50-day (81,252), with 3-month momentum still +29.4% but 1-month momentum -3.0%. It still passes the rule, so it is held at a small 7% weight rather than paying 35bps per side to churn it. If it breaks the 50-day decisively, the next refresh cuts it, and the 20% stop limits the tail.

The dollar trend is mild but intact: UUP at 28.92 is above its 50-day (28.40) and 200-day (27.84) averages, with 3-month momentum of +1.9%. It is a low-volatility (about 5%) diversifier that pays when high US yields draw capital in. The weak momentum argues for keeping it small at 6% with a tight 6% stop.
